takeaway: Consumers turned more upbeat in November. Confidence has risen two months in a row from September's low, and sentiment posted its first gain since July. But both are coming back from weak levels, and November's confidence figure is still preliminary, so treat this as an opening, not a trend. Plan for firmer holiday and early-2027 demand, and keep leading with value, proof and payment options, because price-sensitive shoppers haven't gone away.

slides.label: Retail sales vs. a year ago
slides.bullet: Gas is a big part of the gain: gas station sales are up 27.5% from a year ago. Furniture and home furnishings (+8.5%) outpaced the total, while building materials (+4.2%) and auto dealers (+2.7%) trailed it.
slides.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Monthly Retail Trade (not seasonally adjusted). Released Nov. 17; next release Dec. 16.

chart.title: Retail sales, % change from a year earlier

slides.label: Consumer Confidence Index
slides.bullet: Confidence jumped to its highest level since January 2025 as midterm-election uncertainty faded and gas prices kept falling. The Expectations Index (83.6) rose above 80, the Conference Board's recession-signal line, for the first time this year.
slides.source: The Conference Board, Consumer Confidence Index. Released Nov. 24 (preliminary; final with the December release); October revised to 91.9.

slides.label: Index of Consumer Sentiment
slides.bullet: Sentiment rose to its highest level since August, led by post-election gains in expected business conditions. Falling gas prices helped low- and middle-wealth households, and year-ahead inflation expectations dropped to 3.7% from 4.7%.
slides.source: University of Michigan, Surveys of Consumers. Final November reading released Nov. 20.

slides.label: Fed districts reporting growth
slides.bullet: Consumer spending was little changed in most districts and led by higher-income households. Price-sensitive shoppers are pushing back on increases, squeezing margins for consumer-facing businesses.
slides.source: Federal Reserve Beige Book, released Oct. 14 (information collected through Oct. 5).
